lines.text: Job swears by the living God that his lips will not speak wickedness.
Job vows to maintain his integrity until he dies, and says his conscience will not accuse him.
Job asks what hope the godless have when God takes away their life, and whether God will hear their cry.
The wicked man's many sons are destined for famine, and the plague will bury his survivors.
The wicked man's house is like a moth's cocoon, and the west wind carries him away.
